translations.answer: Maintainer explicitly states that net_forces_w is the net normal contact force in the world frame, and does not include the complete friction component. The old version of the underlying get_friction_data(dt) function requires manual aggregation, and the original author reported full zero results after testing. The official merge of PR #3563 has enabled track_friction_forces and reading friction_forces_w; this field is aggregated by env/body/filter and has official testing. Use this field only after verifying the target version includes PR #3563 and is configured appropriately.
translations.applicability: Applies to Isaac Lab ContactSensor; explicit friction_forces_w path requires the target version to include PR #3563 and be configured to enable friction tracking.
translations.credibility.rationale: The issue has been closed, the environment is clear, and there is no conflict. There is formal documentation or independent reproducible exact reference.
translations.details.attempts.0: The maintainer suggests directly calling contact_physx_view.get_friction_data(dt) and reminds that the format must be manually aggregated.
translations.details.attempts.1: The original author tried the old path and reported full zero, so this path did not form a verified fix in their environment.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: First confirm the semantics of the field: net_forces_w is the net normal contact force in the world frame, not the sum of normal and friction forces.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Confirm whether the target version includes PR #3563, whether track_friction_forces is enabled, the non-empty filter_prim_paths_expr, and valid max_contact_data_count_per_prim.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: In versions containing PR #3563, enable ContactSensorCfg.track_friction_forces and read ContactSensorData.friction_forces_w; the official implementation aggregates friction data by env/body/filter and includes contact/none testing.
translations.details.environments.0: Isaac Lab ContactSensor, long slender cylindrical foot collision geometry; original post does not provide version; PR #3563 was merged into the official repository on 2025-12-10.
translations.details.limits.0: Issue with get_friction_data(dt) in early versions was not successful in the original author's environment, so it cannot be treated as a universal fix.
translations.details.limits.1: The two original graphs do not include Isaac Lab versions, friction coefficient, units, or complete experimental configuration, so the curve size cannot be used to infer real friction parameters.
translations.details.outcomes.0: PR #3563 merged, issue marked as completed; PR testing confirms friction_forces_w is consistent with the underlying get_friction_data aggregation result.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why is net_forces_w only containing normal force when there is clear friction? How to obtain the tangential friction force?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Before using for real-world sliding/friction cone detection, validate coordinate system, sign, filtering, sampling period, and sensor/model errors; simulation contact forces are not substitutes for real-world sensor data.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Reading the compatible net_forces_w field that only carries normal force, but expecting tangential friction force.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Original graph shows z-component of contact foot about 667 N/543 N, while x is about 8e-05/6e-05 and y is zero.
translations.details.symptoms.1: Another user's curve shows only one world axis component varying with dragging, and the other two curves remain at zero.
translations.media_summaries.0: The verified curve from comment 2733805649 shows only the blue X curve varying between -3 and -10 with several peaks, while the orange Y and green Z curves remain at zero; coordinates are only Force/Time with no units, version, or friction parameters, so it only supports the 'other two axes are zero' symptom, not proving force calibration.
translations.media_summaries.1: The MuJoCo screenshot from comment 2752798128 shows multiple shallow blue upward arrows and numerical annotations near the robot's foot, but no legend, coordinate axes, or units; it only expresses the author's desire for a complete contact force visualization, not as a proof of Isaac Lab fix results.
translations.source.locator: IsaacLab #2074: contributor comment 2737575470 explains field semantics; collaborator 2737622128 reminds of output format; original author 2741377794 reports old path full zero; PR #3563 merged into official field

translations.title: Why is net_forces_w in Isaac Lab humanoid footbot only containing normal force, and where to get the tangential friction force?
